response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT e.ordersmark AS ordersmark, o.timespan AS timespan, AVG(e.fillcount) AS avg_fill FROM orderexecutions e JOIN orders o ON e.ordersmark = o.recordvault GROUP BY e.ordersmark, o.timespan), scored AS (SELECT ordersmark, timespan, avg_fill, AVG(avg_fill) OVER (PARTITION BY timespan) AS tif_avg, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY timespan ORDER BY avg_fill DESC NULLS LAST) AS rnk FROM per_order) SELECT ordersmark, timespan, avg_fill, avg_fill - tif_avg AS excess_over_timespan_avg, rnk AS rank_in_timespan FROM scored WHERE avg_fill > tif_avg AND rnk <= 3 ORDER BY timespan, rnk, ordersmark

assumptions.assumption: An order is identified by orders.recordvault (the unique order reference), which equals orderexecutions.ordersmark; the inner join drops unmatched executions.
Orders whose executions all have NULL fillcount have a NULL average; they are left out of the time-in-force mean and cannot pass the strict > filter. Orders with a NULL timespan form their own group.
Rank is computed over all orders in the time in force, before the above-mean filter. This gives the same result as ranking only the kept orders, since those are the highest averages.
